feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 2 (y=0.07 m, 16 mm, ±0.036 m) is the only design that improved on the baseline: score 329 against 140 and 128, oval finish rate 65%, and s-bend progress 0.45. Iteration 1 showed that spread alone (±0.036 m at y=0.04 m) did not reduce line losses (1.05 to 1.1 per run) and cut oval progress, so look-ahead is the lever that has paid off. Iteration 2 also showed steering_oscillation of about 0.28 on the oval and 0.29 on the s-bend, so the forward offset is close to the oscillation limit at kd 0.5. My integration compensation for this geometry is to scale sensor weights to x/0.027 (not x/0.018) so the outer sensors are not clipped, and to raise kp to 4.5 to hold steering gain with the wider spread. Depending on the next race: if line_loss_events fall below 1.0 on s-bend and slalom while steering_oscillation stays at or under 0.3, keep y=0.08 m and try the next step on mass (0.5 kg) to reduce lag. If steering_oscillation rises above 0.3 while line losses fall, move the forward offset back to y=0.06 m with the same spread, because the iteration 2 oscillation level suggests the forward lead is what overshoots. If line losses stay at 1.0 or more and max_error stays near 0.06 m with no oscillation, the limit is actuator lag, not sensing, so change the drivetrain (wheel_track or mass) rather than adding more sensors.
requested_changes: If the next race shows line_loss_events below 1.0 on s-bend and slalom and steering_oscillation at or below 0.3, keep sensor y at 0.08 m and reduce mass from 0.6 to 0.5 kg. Iteration 2 showed that look-ahead cuts max_error, and the remaining limit looks like lag.

If steering_oscillation rises above 0.3 on any track while line losses fall, move all sensor y values from 0.08 to 0.06 m with the same ±0.054 m seven-sensor spread. Iteration 2 already reached 0.28 to 0.29 oscillation at y=0.07 m, so the forward lead is the source of overshoot.

If line_loss_events stay at 1.0 or more and max_error stays near 0.06 m with no oscillation, keep the sensor geometry and try wheel_track 0.09 m for faster turn response. Iterations 1 and 2 showed that spread and footprint changes alone did not remove line losses, so the next lever is drivetrain turn authority.
